title: A New Name, A New Identity

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "As for me, this is my covenant with you: You will be the father of many nations. No longer will you be called Abram; your name will be Abraham, for I have made you a father of many nations." - Gen 17:4-5 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God changes his name. "Abram" means "exalted father" - but Sarai was barren, so for ninety-nine years the name had been almost a cruel irony. Now God renames him "Abraham" - "father of many nations." And here is the wonder: he still has no child of promise. God gives him the new name before the fulfilment, based on what God will surely do.

Imagine introducing yourself as "father of many nations" when you have one son by a slave and a wife long past childbearing. Every time someone said his name, it declared a promise not yet visible. God defined Abraham not by his present circumstances but by God's future purpose for him.

This is how God works with His people. He gives us an identity based not on what we are, but on what He is making us. We may still feel like our old selves - struggling, failing, far from the promise. But God speaks over us who we will be in Him.

In Christ, God gives us new names too: no longer "sinner" but "saint," no longer "orphan" but "child of God," "a new creation" (2 Cor 5:17). One day He promises "a new name" written for each of us (Rev 2:17). Don't let your past or your present define you. Let God's word over your life name you.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Are you defined by your circumstances or by God's word over you?
- What "new name" has God given you in Christ?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, thank You that You define me not by what I am but by what You are making me. Help me live out the new identity You have given me in Christ, believing Your word over my life.
Amen.
